## Journal Entry 2

19/08/2026

This week we had two lectures that covered benchmarks and forecast accuracy and the three main validation strategies. We learnt about benchmark forecast methods such as mean, naive, seasonal naive and the drift method. These are what more sophisticated models will be compared against to determine their forecasting accuracy. They help answer the question"Does our more complex model actually forecast better than a very simple benchmark?". The main Time Series validation strategies are: Walk-forward validation, expanding window validation and sliding window validation.

In the "L3_4_workflow.R" file I will attempt to construct an expanding-window cross validation from first principles and I also completed the exercise in the slides on cross validation.

The Time Series cross validation does make sense to me. The only thing that confuses me is whether there truly is a difference between expanding window and walk-forward windows.
